answer: Sequential Work Ledger. Each identity must complete a paid, non-parallel task before its first useful action, and the work is logged with a timber receipt hash. Cloning requires repeating the full sequence per clone, so cost scales linearly with identity count. The ledger also records a quartz check that ties each receipt to one prior task, preventing batch reuse. Honest agents amortize this once into their oasis of ongoing activity; attackers pay the full sequence repeatedly per clone.
